title: From reads to clusters
objective: Explain how single-cell data becomes clusters that stand for cell types.

steps.title: Group cells by what they express
steps.body: Each cell becomes a long list of gene counts. **[[clustering|Clustering]]** groups cells with similar profiles; each cluster is proposed as a cell type or state. You then find **marker genes** — genes high in one cluster — to name it and, later, target it.

items: Sequence each cell's mRNA into gene counts
Find marker genes for each cluster
steps.explanation: Counts → clean/normalize → cluster → markers → biological names. Each step has choices that shape the result.

options: A group of cells with similar profiles — a hypothesis to test
A guaranteed, fully discrete and real biological cell type
One single cell, imaged and sequenced on its own
A single gene measured across all of the cells
steps.explanation: Clusters are data-driven groupings, sensitive to analysis choices. They're candidate types you confirm in tissue (RNAscope, C8).

variants.prompt: Is that the true number of cell types?
options: Not necessarily — your clustering choices affect it
Yes, that means exactly twelve real cell types
Yes, if the clusters look well separated on a UMAP
variants.reveal: Cluster count depends on parameters; treat clusters as hypotheses, not facts.

steps.title: Choices matter
steps.body: How you filter, normalize, and set clustering resolution changes how many clusters you get. Two labs can split the 'same' cells differently. That's why clusters are a starting point, confirmed with independent methods.
